newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebel chief arrested for car-bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebel chief arrested for car-bomb attack.

text.p: Military intelligence agents arrested a leftist guerrilla leader early on Monday on suspicion of ordering a massive car-bomb attack in northwest Colombia last month, the authorities said.

Ike de Jesus Vergara, allegedly the regional commander of the National Liberation Army (ELN) in the violence-torn banana-growing region of Uraba, was seized in a southern neighbourhood of Bogota, an army spokeswoman said.
He is accused of planning the huge bomb blast which ripped through the heart of Apartado, one of the main towns of Uraba, killing 11 people and injuring 60 others on Feb. 27.

The army also believes Vergara ordered the massacre of nine people in a rural area near the town of Chigorodo last year and led a series of attacks against the army and banana companies which operate in Uraba's so-called "banana belt."

The Apartado car bomb was initially blamed on the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's oldest and largest rebel force. But the army spokeswoman said it was now thought the attack was planned jointly by the FARC and the ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla army which is thought to have only a small presence in Uraba.
Vergara was briefly presented to reporters at a press conference in Bogota on Monday morning in which he denied any links with the Apartado bomb.
